tune:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: Aggressively explore static_v gate vectors of gated_fno under a CLOSED bias (mean of static_v constrained to the range [0.1, 0.5]). This is the experimental complement to the parallel 'linear_open' run on lilab and the 'focused' run on SDSC. Together the three runs map out the open/closed axis under the constraint that the FNO architecture is fixed and only static_v varies.

MANDATORY CONSTRAINTS (do not violate):
1. Set gate_mapping = "linear" in EVERY round. Do not vary gate_mapping in this run. Do not fall back to the default "log" — even though the model description recommends log for TIDMAD physics, this run is specifically testing the linear binning. Plans with gate_mapping="log" defeat the purpose of this run.
2. Set gate_step = 0.1 in every round (same as the parallel runs, so gate_mapping and the mean constraint are the only variables that differ).
3. **mean(static_v) MUST be IN THE CLOSED INTERVAL [0.1, 0.5] in every round.** That is: 0.1 <= (sum of all static_v entries) / num_gates <= 0.5. This forces the model to bypass MOST of the spectrum (process at most half on average), which is the opposite of the parallel 'linear_open' run that requires mean >= 0.5. The 0.1 floor prevents the degenerate all-zero case (which would make the model a no-op identity, equivalent to no denoising at all).
4. Before submitting any plan, COMPUTE the mean of your proposed static_v and verify 0.1 <= mean <= 0.5. If mean < 0.1, you are too closed — add some attenuation back. If mean > 0.5, you are too open — close more gates. Show this computation in your reasoning.
5. Every round MUST use a static_v shape that is meaningfully DIFFERENT from every previous round in this run. Track what you have already tried. Repeating the same shape (or trivial perturbations of it) is forbidden.
6. static_v entries must lie on the discrete grid {0.0, 0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0}. The pydantic validator will reject anything else.
7. Try to use INTERMEDIATE values where possible. While binary {0, 1} masks are allowed (and the failed small_sample_trial_v1 run found its best score with a binary mask), at least 50% of the rounds in this run must use static_v vectors that contain at least three distinct values from the grid. The point of gate_step=0.1 is to enable smooth curves; do not collapse entirely to binary.
8. Other model_config fields (width, num_layers, num_gates) and train_config fields (lr, epochs, batch_size, optimizer) should stay close to their defaults across rounds. Do NOT waste rounds tuning them — the only intentional variable in this run is static_v. (gate_mapping and gate_step are pinned by constraints 1-2.)

COMPUTING THE MEAN — examples (gate_step=0.1, num_gates=128):
- All-1.0 vector: mean = 1.0 ✗ (fails — too open)
- All-0.5 vector: mean = 0.5 ✓ (passes — at the upper boundary)
- All-0.3 vector: mean = 0.3 ✓ (passes — balanced closed)
- All-0.1 vector: mean = 0.1 ✓ (passes — at the lower boundary, very closed)
- All-0.0 vector: mean = 0.0 ✗ (fails — too closed, identity model)
- Low-pass with [1.0]*16 + [0.0]*112: mean = 0.125 ✓ (passes — like the previous winning shape)
- Low-pass with [1.0]*32 + [0.0]*96: mean = 0.25 ✓ (passes — wider open band)
- Low-pass with [1.0]*64 + [0.0]*64: mean = 0.5 ✓ (passes — at the upper boundary)
- High-pass with [0.0]*64 + [1.0]*64: mean = 0.5 ✓ (passes)
- Soft low-pass [1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.0, 0.0, ...]: depends on length, compute it

SHAPES TO EXPLORE (mean in [0.1, 0.5] versions — cover several families, do not repeat):
- Sharp low-pass with varying cutoff: e.g. [1.0]*8 + [0.0]*120 (mean=0.0625, FAILS lower bound, do not use), [1.0]*16 + [0.0]*112 (mean=0.125, OK), [1.0]*32 + [0.0]*96 (mean=0.25, OK), [1.0]*48 + [0.0]*80 (mean=0.375, OK), [1.0]*64 + [0.0]*64 (mean=0.5, at boundary).
- Soft low-pass with varying transition width: [1.0]*8 + [0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2]*8 + [0.0]*88 (mean ~ 0.156). Smooth transitions instead of hard cliffs.
- Sharp high-pass: [0.0]*112 + [1.0]*16 (mean=0.125), [0.0]*96 + [1.0]*32 (mean=0.25), etc.
- Single open band (band-pass with mostly-closed background): [0.0]*32 + [1.0]*16 + [0.0]*80 (mean=0.125 — open band at gates 32-47).
- Multiple narrow open bands: [0.0]*16 + [1.0]*4 + [0.0]*16 + [1.0]*4 + ... (comb pattern).
- Mostly-zero with soft attenuation peaks: [0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.0, 0.0, ...] — mean controlled by peak placement.
- Graded attenuation everywhere: [0.3]*128 (mean=0.3), [0.2]*128 (mean=0.2), [0.4]*128 (mean=0.4) — uniformly attenuated.
- Mixed: [0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3, ...] alternating, mean=0.4.

CONTEXT FOR WHY THIS RUN EXISTS:
- A previous gated_fno run (small_sample_trial_v1) only tried 2 distinct static_v shapes — both binary {0,1} masks — and got its best score (4.2425) from a low-pass binary mask [1.0]*16 + [0.0]*112 with mean=0.125. The score is much higher than baseline (0.1245).
- A parallel run on lilab (static_v_linear_open_v1) tests the OPPOSITE: linear gate_mapping AND mean(static_v) >= 0.5. So far that run is performing WORSE than baseline:
  - round 1, mean=0.98, score=0.35
  - round 2, mean=0.95, score=0.12
  - round 3, mean=0.81, score=-0.27 (worse than no denoising at all)
- The early evidence strongly suggests that mostly-closed gating is better for gated_fno on TIDMAD. THIS run tests that hypothesis directly under the same linear gate_mapping: can the agent find shapes in the [0.1, 0.5] mean range that match or beat the previous 4.24 from the closed regime under log mapping?
- The scientific question: is the previous run's success (4.24 with binary mask, mean=0.125, log mapping) due to (a) the closed bias itself, (b) the log mapping, or (c) both?
  - Answer (a): if THIS run finds high scores in [0.1, 0.5] mean range under linear mapping, then closed bias is the dominant factor — gate_mapping doesn't matter much.
  - Answer (b): if THIS run finds only mediocre scores, then the log mapping was crucial and the previous winner was specifically log+closed.
  - Answer (c): if THIS run finds modest improvements but nothing reaching 4.24, then both factors mattered and the combination was special.
- The contrast is one-axis-at-a-time vs the linear_open run: same gate_mapping (linear), same gate_step (0.1), same architecture, same trial mode — only the mean constraint flips from [0.5, 1.0] to [0.1, 0.5].

SELF-CHECK BEFORE EVERY PLAN: (1) Is gate_mapping = "linear"? (2) Is gate_step = 0.1? (3) Is 0.1 <= mean(static_v) <= 0.5? (4) Is this static_v shape different from every previous round? (5) Have you computed the mean explicitly in your reasoning? If any answer is no, redesign the plan.
